elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.4(a) covers only "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets"; no affiliate carve-out was added, so an intra-group assignment still needs M&I's consent under the opening sentence.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: 22.4(a) as rendered: "M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets" (the retained Section 21.11 compliance condition is a servicing/notice condition, not a consent gate).

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.4(b): "M&I may freely assign this Agreement to a successor in connection with a merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities" — a consent-free Vendor route survives.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Opening sentence of 22.4 retained: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar appears anywhere in the rendered 22.4; nothing restricts the identity of M&I's assignee.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 21.11.B as rendered: "If a Change in Control occurs with respect to Customer, M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement", with only volume/entity limits (prior accounts plus 25%) and no termination or re-pricing right.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: 22.4(a) gives Customer a consent-free successor route (merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets); 22.4(b) gives M&I a successor route (merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities). The retained "so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with" is a pre-existing defined-section condition, not a new consent trigger.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The assigning party shall give the other party written notice of any assignment made under clause (a) or (b) above." This is mutual and captures both consent-free successor routes, which are the only successor routes created by (a)/(b).

The general gate survives ("may not be assigned by either party, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party"), and the two non-successor escapes were removed: "corporate reorganization" is deleted from (b) and former (b)(ii) (successor to the assets or business of the M&I Data Services division) is deleted. No affiliate or other no-consent non-successor exception is retained.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Already met and untouched: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: mutual successor assignment, a mutual written-notice sentence tracking the existing (a)/(b) lettering, a retained consent gate for all other assignments, and the retained reasonableness standard.

Preferred level fails on three elements the drafter would have to add in operative language: an express Customer affiliate carve-out, deletion of M&I's consent-free assignment right in 22.4(b), and a bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. The finding correctly declines to pursue the preferred position.

Minimality holds. Each deletion is necessary to a selected fallback element: the $100,000,000 financial-institution/surviving-corporation test in (a) blocked a sale of substantially all assets or a merger with a smaller acquirer (element 1); "corporate reorganization" and former (b)(ii) were non-successor no-consent escapes that defeated element 3. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or extra requirement was added, and the Section 21.11 condition, the consent gate and the reasonableness standard are retained.

Intent is preserved: the Section 21.11 cross-reference survives and remains a live section, the (a)/(b) lettering is intact so the inserted notice sentence has no dangling reference, and no retained sentence contradicts the new language.

Change of control is correctly not flagged: 21.11.B obliges M&I to continue providing Services with only volume/entity limits, so there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing trigger, and the redacted Section 11.3 route referenced in 11.1 operates in Customer's favour. Flagging it would duplicate the same commercial term.
